title: Trace-Metric Linker and Cold-Start Attribution for Inference Latency
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Create reliable linking between inference metrics (Prometheus/OTel) and distributed traces so on-call and SREs can jump from a high-latency metric point to the exact trace/span that caused it. Extend this to attribute cold-starts (model load, kv-cache miss, compilation jitter) by adding lightweight exemplar and meta-labels at ingest. Motivation: current latency dashboards show spikes but require manual correlation; cold-start incidents often blamed on infra without evidence. This ticket implements exemplar tagging, a sampling policy tuned for production traffic, dashboard query changes, and investigation runbooks for cold-start attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Exemplars are emitted for histogram buckets and summary points for inference latency metrics with trace_id (and span_id when available) without PII
Sampling policy selects exemplars for tail latency (>= p95) and explicit cold-start events (model_load=true) with controlled rate to keep ingestion costs <= 12% increase
Telemetry gateway forwards exemplars to Prometheus remote-write and OTel collector preserving trace linkage
Grafana dashboard panels include a ‘Jump to Trace’ link that opens Jaeger/Tempo for the exemplar trace
Runbook updated with steps to diagnose a cold-start using exemplar trace + metric context
Integration tests validate exemplar presence for synthetic cold-start and tail-latency generators
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Runtime: add an exemplar emission hook in the serving runtime path right after final latency is computed; attach trace_id and span_id attributes and a cold_start boolean label when model load or KV cache miss applies. 2) Sampling: implement deterministic sampling policy in telemetry-fabric: always keep exemplars for requests flagged cold_start, otherwise sample when latency >= p95 or randomly at 0.001 rate for low-volume models. 3) Telemetry pipeline: extend OTLP exporter to carry exemplar attributes and ensure the telemetry-gateway maps them to Prometheus exemplars (exemplar.label.trace_id). 4) Dashboards: add exemplar->trace link templating (prometheus.exemplar_trace_url) and new panel that shows exemplar counts by model+region. 5) Cost control: add guardrails and a throttler in telemetry gateway with per-customer exemplar budget and metrics to monitor exemplar ingestion rate. 6) Privacy: redact any user_text or prompt content; only include trace/ids and inferred labels (model, region, cold_start).
tradeoffs_and_notes: - Pros: fast root-cause (trace) lookup from metric spikes, precise cold-start attribution. - Cons: increased cardinality risk if trace_id becomes a label in downstream systems; mitigated by storing trace_id only as exemplar attribute (Prometheus exemplars are not indexed) and not creating new metric labels. - Performance: minimal extra CPU in hot-path to attach exemplar metadata; we will bench before enabling default on all models. - Cost: remote-write storage will increase due to exemplars metadata; budget set to <=12% for initial rollout. - Alternative considered: push full trace OR span sampling only to tracing backend; rejected because it required more cross-team changes and made metric->trace jump unreliable.
open_questions: Do we want to include span_id for every exemplar, or only when a parent span exists to avoid extra baggage?
What is the exact budget per-customer for exemplar forwarding during peak (suggested 1000 exemplars/min max per tenant)?
Should exemplar sampling be per-model or global? initial plan: global with model overrides via config
Do we need retention changes in Prometheus remote storage for exemplar data? (likely not, exemplars are metadata)
Which teams need explicit opt-in for Private deployments (telemetry collectors that are customer-managed)?
